video_title: 30% of All Bitcoin Exposed to Quantum Computers?

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Google published a quantum result in Science: 40 times fewer errors in one key building block (magic states) on its 105-qubit Willow chip, not a computer 40 times better overall.
claims.evidence_text: On Thursday, Google published a new quantum computing result in the journal Science. 40 times fewer errors in one of the key building blocks for calculations on its quantum chip.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Nine crypto companies warned that 30% of all Bitcoin (about 6 million coins, incl. about 1.1 million attributed to Satoshi) could one day be stolen by a quantum computer.
risks: quantum computers deriving private keys from exposed public keys
claims.evidence_text: On the same day, nine crypto companies warned that 30% of all Bitcoin could one day be stolen by a quantum computer.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Strategy, the biggest corporate holder, owns 848,250 Bitcoin, fewer than the roughly 1.1 million attributed to Satoshi.
claims.evidence_text: At Friday's price, that's about 90 billion dollars, and that's more Bitcoin than Strategy, the biggest corporate holder, owns with 848,250.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: IonQ published a blueprint estimating about 20,000 qubits to break Bitcoin's cryptography on its machine type (26 days per key), versus Google's estimate of fewer than 500,000.
claims.evidence_text: On the 8th of September, IonQ, another quantum computing company, published a blueprint with about 20,000 on a different type of machine.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Prediction-market odds that quantum computers break Bitcoin: 1% by the end of 2026 and 11% by the end of 2027; a tiny market, read only as a mood indicator.
claims.evidence_text: On PolyMarket, a prediction market, the chance that quantum computers break Bitcoin by the end of 2026 is 1%.

claims.speaker: host
claims.reasoning_summary: Satoshi's coins are not in danger this year, but the quantum threat is real enough that the debate (BIP-360/361, freezing old coins) has started; developments could cause at least short-term volatility.
risks: quantum theft of exposed coins, e.g. Satoshi's 1.1 million
freezing old coins would break Bitcoin's core promise
claims.evidence_text: I mean, not this year, and the bettors see it the same way, but the danger is real enough that the fight has already started.
